articles.title: Bread Yeast vs. Microplastics: A Home Experiment with Global Potential
articles.summary: Baker's yeast can act like a natural magnet for microplastics, clumping them so they sink. This experiment lets you test how much yeast is needed to clean contaminated water. It's a hands-on look at bioremediation — using microbes to fight pollution.

articles.title: Cotton-Candy Worlds: Astronomers Discover Two Unbelievably Fluffy Planets
articles.summary: TOI-791 b and c are Jupiter-sized but have densities lower than cotton candy. Found by citizen scientists and confirmed with Antarctic telescope data, these rare super-puff planets orbit in a 5:3 resonance. They challenge our understanding of planet formation.

articles.title: Underground Allies: How Root Bacteria Fortify Crops Against Salty Soil
articles.summary: Pseudomonad bacteria naturally gather on roots under salt stress, boosting plant growth without reducing internal salt levels. This discovery could lead to microbial treatments for crops on salt-damaged farmland, a growing threat to global food supplies.
